newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Jan consumer prices rise 2.2 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Canada Jan consumer prices rise 2.2 pct on year.

text.p: Canada's unadjusted January consumer price index rose 0.2 percent in the month and 2.2 percent in the year to 137.1, Statistics Canada said Friday.
CONSUMER PRICES - Pct chg Jan Dec
Unadjusted ex food and energy mth/mth +0.1 +0.0
Unadjusted ex food and energy yr/yr +1.8 +1.8

A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unadjusted CPI to rise 0.25 percent on the month. The survey also forecast a 2.2 percent year-over-year rise in the all-items and 0.15 percent month-on-month rise in the core CPI.
The core CPI rise of 1.8 percent on the year was comfortably within the Bank of Canada's target range of one to three percent.

The month-on-month 0.2 percent increase in the unadjusted CPI was due to higher prices for phone services (+5.7 percent), food, piped gas, women's clothing and cablevision. Food rose 0.5 percent, a relatively small increase for January, and energy rose 0.7 percent.
But mortgage interest charges fell 0.8 percent, and travel tours, footwear, new vehicles and air transportation were lower.

The year-on-year unadjusted increase was due to higher prices for transportation, food, university tuition and phone services. But this was moderated by a 5.2 percent decline in mortage interest charges. Energy rose 6.2 percent on the year, and food 2.2 percent.
